Sentinel — security correlation and response

Sentinel turns FortiWeb attack-log events, HTTP outcomes, appliance and infrastructure metrics and vulnerability data into scored incidents that explain themselves, and proposes — never silently performs — responses.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view protection.apply
📍 WhereGlobal ADOM → Monitoring → Sentinel (URL /sentinel/); settings in Settings → Sentinel; architecture page at /sentinel/docs

What is it?#

Sentinel answers "what is actually happening right now, across every layer at once?". It reads the FortiWeb attack log and traffic outcomes, lines them up with appliance, VM, hypervisor and backend metrics and with a local copy of vulnerability intelligence, and groups related events into incidents with a score from 0 to 100. Every number on an incident can be traced back to its evidence. When a response is warranted, Sentinel proposes it; whether anything is ever executed is decided by the response policy, a set of gates, and — in most configurations — a person.

What does it do?#

  • Collects FortiWeb attack-log events in sweeps (run on demand or by the sentinel_sweep scheduled action). FortiADC appliances are not swept — they have no attack log.
  • Correlates events into incidents (reference INC-<year>-<number>), with a timeline, an evidence table and time-aligned charts of every layer.
  • Scores each incident with a fixed, published weight table, including factors that lower the score (for example, a WAF that is already answering 403). A behavioural baseline (per hour of the week) is used once it has learned enough; immature buckets never fire.
  • Proposes responses from a closed catalogue (such as blocking an address, raising protection, blocking a country, listing an address on a border blocklist, tuning a signature) and shows every gate that allowed or refused each one.
  • Optional AI opinion: a local model can add a narrative and an assessment, clearly labelled as a model's opinion. It cannot change the score or the decision.
  • Publishes an optional border blocklist that an external firewall can fetch.

Score bands#

Score Band Meaning
below 40 observe Recorded; no action proposed
40–69 investigate Worth a look
70–84 recommend An action is recommended to a person
85 and above semi_auto Eligible for semi-automatic response, if the policy allows it

The pages#

Page URL What it shows
Console /sentinel/ Pipeline health (last sweep, baseline coverage, CVE mirror, response engine), 7-day statistics, and the incident list with Live, Closed, False positives and All filters
Incident /sentinel/incident/<id> How this score was reached, Evidence, Every layer, same time axis, Model assessment, Timeline, Response (with each gate), Border blocklist, Seen before?, Close, and the raw Events
Context /sentinel/context Trusted sources, maintenance windows, topology (appliance ↔ VM ↔ host ↔ backend), the border map, the local CVE mirror and Response arming
Response policy /sentinel/policies Operating mode, the global kill switch, the per-action policy table and recent decisions
Border blocklist /sentinel/blocklist Feed status, token, audit mirror, manual listing and the current entries
Architecture /sentinel/docs How Sentinel works, rendered from the running code (see The architecture page)

The same sections are also available in Settings → Sentinel (Settings, Context, Response policy, Border blocklist, Architecture, Incidents console).

Requirements#

  • Sentinel switched on in Settings → Sentinel → Settings (on by default; AI reasoning is off by default). While Sentinel is off the console reads disabled and sweeps are refused.
  • FortiWeb appliances SATOM can read.
  • For behavioural factors: SATOM's local metrics store must be up. When it is not, the console shows Metrics store unreachable and behavioural factors are absent from scores (not zero).
  • For VM and host layers: a topology row on the Context page; without one those layers are reported as unknown.

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the console, incidents, context, architecture page monitoring.view
Run sweep now, Recompute from the store, Re-correlate, Ask the model, Record decision, Close incident Configuration-write — for example protection.apply, protection.edit, network.apply, operations.apply or appliances.apply
Context changes (trusted sources, windows, topology, border map, arming, CVE sync) Configuration-write
Response policy and Border blocklist pages and their changes Configuration-write
Open Settings → Sentinel and its demo scenarios The legacy view gate — any read permission, for example monitoring.view
Settings → Sentinel (save) Configuration-write

The seeded operator and admin profiles have configuration-write; the readonly profile can read but every button returns 403. The Sentinel menu entry is only offered in the Global ADOM. The console, its live refresh and the incident page show only incidents of appliances visible to you in the current ADOM; an incident of an appliance you cannot see is not shown, even by its address.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the console's live refresh and the incident page no longer show incidents of appliances you cannot see, the Sentinel pages need monitoring.view, and Settings → Sentinel needs a read permission instead of sign-in alone.

How to use#

Run a sweep#

  1. Open Monitoring → Sentinel in the Global ADOM.
  2. Click Run sweep now. The Run a sweep window lists FortiWeb appliances; ones in maintenance or with a retired host are shown but cannot be selected.
  3. Pick devices (Select all / Select none; nothing selected means every eligible device) and click Start sweep.
  4. The sweep runs as a job: Sweep started as job N over M device(s). Progress is in the Jobs dock; this page does not wait for it. See Jobs.

Work an incident#

  1. In Incidents, click Open on an incident.
  2. Read How this score was reached and Evidence. Use Re-correlate to rebuild them from current data.
  3. Optional: Ask the model for an AI assessment (only if AI reasoning is enabled in settings).
  4. In Response, expand an action to see each gate, add a note and click Record decision. An allowed action is queued for the response runner, which re-checks every gate before writing anything; a refused one is recorded as rejected with the reason.
  5. Close it under Close: choose closed — handled, mitigated — an action worked or false positive. A false positive needs a reason from Why it was a false positive; add a Note and click Close incident.

Choose an operating mode#

  1. Open Response policy.
  2. Under Operating mode, review the four presets — Alert only, Alert and block, High, Ultra high — and their Risk notes.
  3. Click Apply <mode>. A mode only writes values into the existing settings and policy rows; edit any of them afterwards and the posture reads Custom.

❗Important

No mode changes AI consent, vulnerability-feed consent, the never-block list or hardened profiles. Blocking a country never goes beyond recommend, even in Ultra high. An action whose mechanism has not been verified against a live appliance executes nothing in any mode.

The architecture page#

/sentinel/docs (also Settings → Sentinel → Architecture) explains the design in twelve numbered sections — the two paths (deterministic pipeline vs. optional AI), diagrams, correlation layers, the baseline, the live weight table and bands, HTTP outcomes and vulnerability intelligence, the response catalogue and gate order, the AI wall and its allowed answers, false-positive reasons, attack families, every setting and what it changes, and the scheduled actions that run it. Tables on that page are generated from the running code, so they always match the installed version.

Result#

  • Incidents, evidence, actions and decisions are kept in SATOM's database; the timeline of each incident records every decision and who made it.
  • Arming a policy for enforcement is written to the audit log as sentinel.arm.
  • Scheduled actions: sentinel_sweep, sentinel_baseline, sentinel_vuln_sync, sentinel_feed_publish. Queued actions are executed by the separate response runner service. See Scheduled actions.

Troubleshooting#

"Sentinel is disabled in Settings — nothing was collected."#

Possible causes - Sentinel is switched off.

Solution 1. Switch it on in Settings → Sentinel → Settings (configuration-write).

"Every device you picked is in maintenance or retired — a sweep would skip all of them, so none was started."#

Possible causes - Only ineligible appliances were selected.

Solution 1. Take the appliance out of maintenance, or pick other devices.

The Pipeline tile says "never run"#

Possible causes - No sweep heartbeat has reached the metrics store yet.

Solution 1. Run a sweep, or schedule the sentinel_sweep action.

Verification - The tile shows Ns ago.

"AI reasoning is disabled in Settings — the incident keeps its deterministic score and evidence."#

Possible causes - AI reasoning is off in Sentinel settings.

"… refused by the policy engine: …"#

Possible causes - A gate refused the action (kill switch, band, rate limit, never-block list, unarmed policy…). The reason is shown and recorded on the timeline.

"… approved and recorded, but NOT queued: its mechanism has never been run against a live appliance of this product, so there is nothing to execute."#

Possible causes - The action's transport is not verified. This is by design.

"a false positive must record why it was one"#

Possible causes - false positive was chosen without a reason.

"Never-block list has unparseable entries"#

Possible causes - A line in the never-block list is not a valid address or range. Those lines protect nothing.

Solution 1. Fix them in Settings → Sentinel.

Advanced#

Advanced Where to read more

The full design — scoring factors, gate order, operating-mode presets, border corroboration and the blocklist feed — is described on the architecture page of your installation. For the background services involved, see Services and timers.

Advanced What never happens

A page view never contacts an appliance. Approving an action only queues it; the runner re-evaluates every gate at execution time and confirms the result by re-reading the device. Response arming (binding Sentinel's list to a policy's protection profile) is a separate, explicit, audited operator action.
